We continued IV ceftriaxone here and her respiratory status slowly improved during the course of her hoshave weaned her off the oxygen today and she is doing reasonably well on room air with ambulation. Patient presents with abdominal pain found to have 9 mm obstructing left-sided nephrolithiasis and transferred to Scripps Mercy Hospital for urology consultation. Continue antibiotics, follow blood cultures. UA unremarkable although, in the setting of obstructive disease as above likely infection proximal to renal stone. However, urine culture ordered from urine specimen prior to antibiotic administration. -CT A/P without contrast noting 9 mm obstructive nephrolithiasis with left hydronephrosis and left perinephric stranding. The patient was placed on IV ceftriaxone and was evaluated by Urology Dr. Holden. -The patient was taken to the OR for a cystoscopy and stent placement. Cultures were obtained intra-op. She has done well post-op after the stent placement and had the foley removed and had good urine output without significant hematuria. The patient was cleared to go home from Urology standpoint on 4/22 with PO abx and follow up with eventual plan to remove the stent in several weeks. We will send her with 7 days of PO abx. Aspiration event- the patient likely had an aspiration event after extubation in the PACU. She was having increasing cough with phlegm and some hypoxia necessitating NC O2. She was slowly weaned down from NC O2 and we did have Pulmonary Medicine consult on her 4/21. We are continuing Ceftriaxone and nebulizer treatments as well as supplemental oxygen and she looks better today. The likely culprit is aspiration pneumonitis without clear PNA. She is still having some hypoxia so we are continuing NC O2 at this point in time. We continued IV ceftriaxone here and her respiratory status slowly improved during the course of her hospital stay. We have weaned her off the oxygen today and she is doing reasonably well on room air with ambulation. PT/OT worked with her on stairs and she has done well. She will go home today with 7 days of PO Ceftin to complete treatment course. Acute renal failure No previous creatinine to review in epic other than back in 2018 which demonstrated normal creatinine. Will continue IVF and monitor creatinine daily. Her CR bumped up to 1.98 during the hospital stay. Today it is down to 1.45 and she has good urine output. Type 2 diabetes Patient hyperglycemic upon arrival. Hold oral antihyperglycemics. Give low-dose Lantus and sliding scale insulin. -Lantus 5 units daily, SSI. She will remain on IVF for the time being and her sugar levels are still elevated. She had a swallow evaluation and was cleared to have regular texture diet. A diet was resumed 4/21 and she is tolerating that reasonably well. We are continuing SSI and accuchecks for her. Hypertension with hypertensive urgency upon arrival to the ED Blood pressure 194/87 upon arrival to the ED. Blood pressure downtrended over the next several hours and now 112/82. Possible bowel early sepsis. Holding antihypertensive therapies. Her BP has normalized and is now elevated. Will restart amlodipine and order hydralazine for PRN control. Her BP control has improved over the past 24 hours. Discharge Medications: Amoxicillin.

Patient presents with abdominal pain found to have 7 mm obstructing left-sided nephrolithiasis and transferred to Scripps Mercy Hospital for urology consultation. Continue antibiotics, follow blood cultures. UA unremarkable although, in the setting of obstructive disease as above likely infection proximal to renal stone. However, urine culture ordered from urine specimen prior to antibiotic administration. -CT A/P without contrast noting 7 mm obstructive nephrolithiasis with left hydronephrosis and left perinephric stranding. The patient was placed on IV ceftriaxone and was evaluated by Urology Dr. Holden. -The patient was taken to the OR for a cystoscopy and stent placement. Cultures were obtained intra-op. She has done well post-op after the stent placement and had the foley removed and had good urine output without significant hematuria. The patient was cleared to go home from Urology standpoint on 4/22 with PO abx and follow up with eventual plan to remove the stent in several weeks. We will send her with 7 days of PO abx. Aspiration event- the patient likely had an aspiration event after extubation in the PACU. She was having increasing cough with phlegm and some hypoxia necessitating NC O2. She was slowly weaned down from NC O2 and we did have Pulmonary Medicine consult on her 4/21. We are continuing Ceftriaxone and nebulizer treatments as well as supplemental oxygen and she looks better today. The likely culprit is aspiration pneumonitis without clear PNA. She is still having some hypoxia so we are continuing NC O2 at this point in time. We continued IV ceftriaxone here and her respiratory status slowly improved during the course of her hospital stay. We have weaned her off the oxygen today and she is doing reasonably well on room air with ambulation. PT/OT worked with her on stairs and she has done well. She will go home today with 7 days of PO Ceftin to complete treatment course. Acute renal failure No previous creatinine to review in epic other than back in 2018 which demonstrated normal creatinine. Will continue IVF and monitor creatinine daily. Her CR bumped up to 1.45 during the hospital stay. Today it is down to 0.88 and she has good urine output. Type 2 diabetes Patient hyperglycemic upon arrival. Hold oral antihyperglycemics. Give low-dose Lantus and sliding scale insulin. -Lantus 5 units daily, SSI. She will remain on IVF for the time being and her sugar levels are still elevated. She had a swallow evaluation and was cleared to have regular texture diet. A diet was resumed 4/21 and she is tolerating that reasonably well. We are continuing SSI and accuchecks for her. Hypertension with hypertensive urgency upon arrival to the ED Blood pressure 218/79 upon arrival to the ED. Blood pressure downtrended over the next several hours and now 112/71. Possible bowel early sepsis. Holding antihypertensive therapies. Her BP has normalized and is now elevated. Will restart amlodipine and order hydralazine for PRN control. Her BP control has improved over the past 24 hours. Discharge Medications: Amoxicillin.
